notes: §1985:VIII.3.2.4 GR4: 'The LABEL RECORDS clause for the Relative I-O module is the same as the LABEL RECORDS clause for the Sequential I-O module', i.e. §1985:VII.3.6: LABEL {RECORD IS | RECORDS ARE} {STANDARD | OMITTED}, label content the implementor's (no labels processed, docs/CONFORMANCE.md 3.7), and GR4's 'all LABEL RECORDS clauses in the run unit which are associated with this file connector must have the same specification'. CobolData.g4#labelRecordsClause is that format; FileControlBinder#CaptureLabelRecords records the specification and ExternalFileConnectorRules#CheckFileDescriptions compares external entries at 85 (COBOL6847); VersionConformancePass#VisitLabelRecordsClause refuses the clause from 2002 (COBOL0902). Probes at --std 85 on a relative file: LABEL RECORD IS OMITTED (RANDOM) and LABEL RECORDS STANDARD (DYNAMIC) compile and run (failed OPEN INPUT of a missing file gives status 35, then write and random READ give 00 REC3); LABEL RECORDS ARE HDR and ARE IGNORED refused (COBOL5506), the clause twice refused (COBOL2423); an EXTERNAL relative file STANDARD in one program and OMITTED in the other refused (COBOL6847), STANDARD in both or RECORD IS / RECORDS ARE spellings accepted; at --std 2002 refused COBOL0902. The witness writes and reads a sequential-access relative file under LABEL RECORDS ARE STANDARD.

next.reason: 1985: "The LABEL RECORDS clause is an obsolete element in Standard COBOL because it is to be deleted from the next revision"; 2023: "No LABEL RECORDS clause: the 13.4.5 file description entry rules name BLOCK CONTAINS, CODE-SET, LINAGE, RECORD, REPORT only". 1985 marked LABEL RECORDS obsolete and due for deletion. The 2023 FD rules cover the other FD clauses and none states or mentions LABEL RECORDS, so the clause is dropped.
